universal_lens: Motion entropy as time-varying signal feature enables event-based segmentation via homoscedastic change point detection in sports video sequences. EMV-based change point detection unifies motion entropy and temporal segmentation for semantically significant event identification.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference on motion entropy curves supports probabilistic event classification and temporal localization in video skimming pipelines. Bayesian inference models EMV as posterior likelihood over event hypotheses, conformal prediction bounds uncertainty in segmentation thresholds.
gse_mapping: Situation-aware state transitions track motion pattern evolution across semantically significant play segments in real-time sports video processing. Situational reasoning maps EMV peaks to state transitions between game phases; state-transition graph encodes dynamic event clustering.

primitives.name: Motion Entropy Characterization
primitives.verbatim_quote: By applying a homoscedastic error model-based time series change point detection algorithm to this motion entropy curve, one is able to segment the corresponding video sequence into individual sections, each consisting of a semantically relevant event.
primitives.assumptions: Motion entropy varies smoothly over time; change points correspond to semantic events.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When motion entropy exceeds threshold variance, indicating abrupt motion dynamics.

primitives.name: Simple Decision Rule
primitives.verbatim_quote: For each candidate sport event segment, if the corresponding impact value IVal > 0, then it is semantically significant.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes that the increase in activity during an event outweighs the subsequent decay, indicating net positive engagement.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when pre-event buildup mimics post-event decay, leading to reversed classification.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI binary hypothesis testing framework, where H0: IVal ≤ 0 represents background noise and H1: IVal > 0 represents a signal.

primitives.name: Accumulated Impact Value
primitives.verbatim_quote: To quantify this empirically determined rule, an accumulated impact value IVal is defined as the difference between the curve increasing from the starting to the peak (PIVal) and the curve decreasing from the peak (with maximum value) to the end (NIVal) for each event segment.

primitives.assumptions: Assumes that the area under the rising edge minus the falling edge quantifies the net contribution of the event.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when the event produces a flat plateau rather than a sharp peak, resulting in cancellation errors.
